Hi Naomi,

Tried to accept the vendor invite this morning and hit a couple of problems: after I click the link it briefly opens the claim page, then I get bounced to a different tenant and the OTP page says my code has expired. I took a screenshot attached.

Steps I took:
- Clicked the invite link from your email (attached)
- Landed on claim page for "SupplyWorks"
- Redirected (fast) to a tenant labeled "supplyworks-eu" in the URL
- OTP input rejects the code with "expired" even though I just generated it from the email

This is blocking our procurement team — can you reissue or suggest a workaround?

Attachments: invite-link.txt, otp-screenshot.png

Thanks,
Jordan Mills

Subject: Re: SupplyWorks invite — keep getting redirected and OTP expires

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear steps and the screenshot, that helps.

Short answer: this looks like a tenant-routing redirect + OTP TTL/cookie timing issue. Two things we'll try immediately:

1) Quick workaround (please try):
- Open the invite link in an incognito window and *do not* let the browser follow any automatic redirects. If you see a small blue banner that mentions region/tenant, click "claim for SupplyWorks (US)" instead of letting it auto-redirect.
- If the OTP page still rejects codes, reply to this thread with the exact timestamp shown on the OTP error page; that helps us correlate with logs.

2) Our side: Ben and I will escalate to infra to check the tenant mapping and the OTP TTL. If needed we'll reissue an invite with a longer claim window and an alternate anchor URL that avoids the redirect.

Can you confirm whether your team usually receives invites to a shared mailbox or an individual address?

I'll follow up with a Jira ticket and a trace-id once Ben grabs logs.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Manager, Partner Onboarding | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SupplyWorks invite — keep getting redirected and OTP expires

Forwarding Jordan's note — I created an on-call ticket and grabbed the initial trace. Notes:

- Trace id: trace-20261030-7346 (attached in trace-id.txt)
- Observed a 307 redirect from claims.redwood.com to claims.redwood.com/tenant/supplyworks-eu when the invite query contains region=auto.
- OTP generation looks normal but the frontend is validating against a cookie-bound timestamp; there is a ~90s skew in the cookie TTL for requests that come through the redirect chain. That explains "expired" despite freshly submitted codes.

Action plan:
- Short term (today): Naomi, reissue invite using the manual-claim parameter (we'll send a link without region=auto). That should avoid tenant auto-handoff.
- Medium term: Engineering will patch the redirect handler to preserve the original claim timestamp (ONB-4921). I've linked the Jira.

I've cc'd the infra lead on the ticket. Rachel, can you coordinate the reissue and include a note about the manual steps in the email?

Ben
Ben Carter
Staff Engineer, Reliability | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SupplyWorks invite — keep getting redirected and OTP expires

Jordan — sorry again for the friction, and thanks for the quick replies.

What we did for you:
- Reissued a new invite (link below) that omits region=auto and includes manual-claim=true, with an extended OTP window (20 minutes).
- Temporary anchor URL: https://claims.redwood.com/claim?supplier=supplyworks&manual-claim=true
- Please open in a private/incognito window. Steps: open link -> select "Claim for SupplyWorks (US)" if prompted -> use the code in the invite email within 20 minutes.

If that still fails: reply with the exact text of the OTP error and the timestamp shown on the page. We'll pull the trace (trace-20261030-7346) and correlate.

I'll keep ONB-4921 open until the engineering fix deploys; Ben has added notes about preserving the original claim timestamp.

Thanks for your patience — let me know when you've accepted and we will continue the PO setup.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
